thread:
Anya Lopez: quick brain dump — i sketched a connector pattern where the control plane terminates inside customer VPC (no peering) and we talk outbound to a regional relay. want tradeoffs + migration plan ideas. TL;DR: avoid cross-account peering but keep SLOs.

Kevin Patel: +1 to avoiding peering for ops simplicity. main concerns: latency bump, egress IP stability for customers that rely on allowlists, and auth handshake. how do you plan cert rotation? :thinking:

Anya Lopez: good call. rotation would be short-lived mTLS creds minted by our controlplane sts and delivered via the connector agent. agent rotates locally, uses local KMS for ephemeral keys. thought: use an allowlist token that maps to customer ARN to avoid static IP reliance.

Sara Kim: curious about failure modes — if relay is regional and we lose connectivity, do we fallback to peering? that was a previous ask from infra.

Anya Lopez: we can define fallback tiers: 1) regional relay (normal), 2) alternate relay in another AZ/region, 3) optional customer-initiated peering (manual enable). default is no peering. fallback should be opt-in for customers who need absolute latency.

Kevin Patel: operationally, customers with strict egress allowlists will need stable egress IPs. we could support an "egress-preserve" flag on the connector which requests an assigned elastic IP on our managed NAT gateway used for that customer. that adds cost but keeps allowlist compatibility.

Mike Chen: migration plan note: avoid a big-bang. propose 3-stage rollout: 1) test pilot customers with non-critical workloads, 2) internal services + opt-in customers, 3) default for all new tenants + migration script for existing. add monitoring: tail latency P50/P95, connection churn, TLS errors, and a canary that exercises KV cache to detect degraded inference traffic.

Sara Kim: also surface diagnostics in Console: connection age, last-rotation, egress-ip (if assigned), and relay hop count. ops page should have one-click fallback to enable peering for a tenant.

Anya Lopez: agree. interface boundary question: what does the connector agent API expose? my proposal: minimal RPC surface — Register(session_meta), Heartbeat(state), FetchConfig(), PushMetrics(bundle). nothing else (no SSH, no direct admin). docs stub: 

```
# Connector CRD (sketch)
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: tenant-123-connector
spec:
  mode: "outbound-relay" # options: outbound-relay | peering | hybrid
  preserveEgress: false
  allowedCIDRs: []
  keystore: "local-kms"

status:
  lastSeen: "2024-11-05T12:23:00Z"
  egressIP: "34.123.45.67"
  relayRegion: "us-west-2"
```

Kevin Patel: thank you for the sketch. keep config small. we should ensure connector only accepts signed policies from control plane. also add a "maxBatchSize" hint for inference optimizations (so runtime can adjust batching).

Mike Chen: rollback story: keep traffic splitters at load-balancer level so we can route a small percent to old peered controlplane path. plus a kill-switch feature flag in Console that flips to peering for a tenant. Practice cutover during low-traffic windows.

Sara Kim: security question — how do we validate outbound relays? need to ensure customers can't MITM our controlplane. mTLS + token at TCP layer plus service identity checks. ArchBot: scanning known issues — previous peering-based model used cross-account IAM roles; moving to outbound relays removes that surface but adds egress auditing complexity. recommended: include audit log stream from connector to customer's S3 (opt-in) and to our audit pipeline (masked).

Anya Lopez: good. next steps: 1) write an RFC that lists interface contract + minimal CRD + rotation lifecycle, 2) prototype connector with local keystore and relay handshake, 3) run 2 pilot customers for 4 weeks. i'll draft RFC early next week. tagging @Kevin and @Sara for review. :thumbsup:

Kevin Patel: sounds good. i'll mock up the heartbeat schema and failure states.

Sara Kim: i'll add Console wireframes for the tenant page and the kill-switch.

ArchBot: note — created a follow-up issue INFRA-2873: "connector: outbound-relay migration RFC + pilot".

Mike Chen: ping when RFC lands, i'll schedule pilot rollout plan and on-call playbook.

Anya Lopez: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open for async comments.
